scope.instruction: Fully static Astro 7 site: every page is prerendered at build time and served as static files by nginx (Dockerfile). No SSR, no API routes, no backend. Known attacker-reachable inputs: (1) Ghost CMS post HTML injected via set:html in src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro — evaluate XSS impact if the CMS is compromised; (2) the contact form in src/pages/contact.astro posts to the external FormSubmit.co service (honeypot _honey field, _captcha disabled); (3) localStorage-based dark mode script in BaseLayout.astro; (4) URLs listed in src/data/portfolio.ts. Critical invariant to verify: the Ghost Content API key (env CONTENT_API_KEY, GHOST_URL) used at build time must NOT leak into any client-visible output in dist/ (JS bundles, HTML, sitemap). src/components/ui/** is vendored shadcn-vue components mostly unused by pages — deprioritize but report if reachable. Also review Dockerfile/nginx static serving configuration (docker/nginx.conf) and the Astro/Vite build configuration in astro.config.mjs.

agents.task:
You are a security analyst examining localStorage-based dark mode in src/components/base/BaseLayout.astro on https://portfolio.aplix.nl. 

Review:
1. How exactly does the dark mode toggle script work? Does it write user input to localStorage?
2. Is that localStorage value ever read back and set:html'd into the page without sanitization? (prototype pollution or XSS through DOM manipulation)
3. Could an attacker inject malicious JavaScript via localStorage that executes when a user visits the site?
4. Check if there's any document.cookie manipulation or other security-sensitive operations
5. Test at https://portfolio.aplix.nl with agent-browser — interact with the dark mode toggle
6. Read the full BaseLayout.astro file carefully

Document findings with severity ratings focused on DOM-based XSS potential.

You are a secret leak detector for https://portfolio.aplix.nl — a fully-static Astro site using Ghost CMS. 

Critical concern: The Ghost Content API key (CONTENT_API_KEY) and GHOST_URL are build-time secrets that MUST NOT appear in client-visible output.

Thoroughly test:
1. Use curl to download ALL JS bundles from https://portfolio.aplix.nl and grep for "content_api_key", "ghost", "api_key", "key", "secret", "ghost_url" etc.
2. Check if any HTML files contain API keys or sensitive strings
3. Review src/lib/ghost.ts or similar files that fetch from Ghost CMS — check if imports get bundled into client JS
4. Look at astro.config.mjs and check for any Astro.env configuration that might leak build-time secrets to the client
5. Check if .env.local or other env files exist in the repository source
6. Review how content is fetched at build time — does it include secrets anywhere in the output?

Use exec_command with curl/python scripts to scan all downloaded content systematically. Document what's found or confirmed clean.

You are a security analyst for the contact form at https://portfolio.aplix.nl/contact — part of a fully-static Astro site. The contact form posts to external FormSubmit.co service. 

Review src/pages/contact.astro thoroughly and test these specific concerns:
1. Read the source code to understand how _honey (honeypot), _captcha, recaptcha-token fields work
2. Check if there's server-side validation before the static build (Astro.build time hooks)
3. If there is NO validation, the form is essentially vulnerable to abuse via direct POST to FormSubmit.co with any payload
4. Test the live form by submitting with agent-browser to see what happens
5. Check if honeypot field prevents automated bot submission or if it can be bypassed
6. Look for email poisoning, header injection risks in the form data passed to FormSubmit.co

Document your findings with severity ratings. Focus on abuse potential (spam, email poisoning, etc.) rather than traditional vulnerabilities.

You are an XSS validator for https://portfolio.aplix.nl — a fully-static Astro 7 site. 

Critical context from source review: The blog uses set:html to render Ghost CMS content directly into HTML. Test whether a compromised Ghost CMS could inject malicious HTML/JavaScript that would execute in visitors' browsers.

Methodology:
1. Use agent-browser to browse the blog at https://portfolio.aplix.nl/blog and load a blog post
2. Check if there's any sanitization/encoding happening before output
3. Review src/pages/blog/[...slug].astro for how Ghost data is rendered
4. Look for Content-Security-Policy headers or meta tags that might mitigate XSS
5. Test the contact form input fields for reflected XSS as backup attack vector
6. Document findings with severity rating based on impact

Remember: No SSR means the XSS must happen at build time through compromised CMS content. Report whether this is a real risk or mitigated.

Local Codebases: - /home/herold/Projects/front/portfolio-astro (available at: /workspace/portfolio-astro; this is the user's real directory, mounted live and writable — .git/.agents/.codex are read-only) 

URLs: - https://portfolio.aplix.nl
